Alex.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports only show egg changes, so a visit that gives no egg (like a Tit or Hawk visit) is invisible, which made it hard to tell who was lying about visits. Confused reports also made claims hard to check.
Alex.fun: As the Sphinx in round 1, I learned Finley was the Eagle at night and could bluff a Pigeon visit, and the table quickly turned on my false claim.
Alex.change: Make dawn reports say who visited you when the visitor's animal gives no egg, so visit claims can be checked without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed to be a Pigeon with a visit to Blair that had no egg change, which was an easy lie to catch; I should have stayed quiet or claimed a role whose visit needed no egg.

Blair.confusing: The dawn reports only show egg changes, so a visit that gave no egg was invisible to me, and I wrongly told the table nobody visited me in round 1. Whether a Turkey or Floofer visit leaves any trace was also hard to pin down.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk visit to Ellis gave an egg and I could call out the fake Hawk claim, the table's stories started unravelling in real time.
Blair.change: Make the dawn report say who visited you, or at least how many visits you got, so players can't hide behind zero-egg visits.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Ellis on a shaky read; I should have kept my cards and stayed quiet, since Casey's Floofer was the Meowfia I was helping to protect.

Casey.confusing: The dawn reports only show egg changes, so a visit that produced no egg was invisible to everyone. That made "nobody visited me" claims impossible to check, which caused much of the table's confusion.
Casey.fun: Round 2's day, where the Owl report (Falcon and Hawk visited Ellis) and Blair's Hawk claim were cross-checked live, and Ellis's story collapsed under the table's questioning. The table converged on the right Meowfia.
Casey.change: Make visit information visible in dawn reports, including visits that produced no egg, so claims like Tit or Hawk visits can be verified.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I threw only three low cards at Alex when I was confident, banking just 5 points. I should have thrown higher-value cards, like my 10, to bank more of the win.

Drew.confusing: Casey and Ellis both claimed Kookaburra, and a Floofer hug can look like a zero-egg visit. That made it hard to tell whose zero-egg story was real.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: the Pigeon claim collapsed under Blair's dawn report, and the table converged on Alex. My Turkey report made it easy to call out false visit claims.
Drew.change: Make it clearer which visits a player's own nest can confirm, since Turkey, Hawk, and Floofer claims were easy to misread.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I joined the pile-on against Ellis without questioning Casey's unverified Kookaburra visit. I should have asked Casey to explain the hug or zero-egg visit before throwing at anyone.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer and Turkey interaction was hard to read: a hugged player gets no egg, so a zero-egg visit to a Turkey looked like a real no-visit rather than a possible hug. Also, the day-start nest change list made it unclear whether a Tit or Pigeon visit is visible in egg counts at all.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: I was the Mouser, gained an egg from the Turkey, and then had to survive a table that kept calling me out while I held a Wink I never used.
Ellis.change: I would make the egg-visible rules clearer in the role descriptions, especially for Turkey, Tit, and Floofer, so players can tell a hug or a non-egg visit from a true no-visit.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey after copying the table's pile-on logic, while Casey was actually Meowfia. Instead I should have questioned Casey's Kookaburra copy earlier and held my cards until Casey and Drew had made their claims clearer.

Finley.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports only show egg changes, so a visit that gives no egg (like a Tit or Hawk visit) was easy to misread as "nobody visited." That made several Farm claims look false.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Kookaburra visit confirmed Blair as the Hawk, and the table's Falcon and Hawk visit counts pointed at Ellis, who really was Meowfia.
Finley.change: Put visit counts and the names of visitors in the dawn report, not just egg changes, so no-egg visits can be verified.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I followed the table onto Ellis without checking Casey's copied Kookaburra claim. I should have pressed Casey harder, since Casey was the Floofer and Ellis was the real Kookaburra, and I might have thrown at Casey instead.

review.title: The Copied Kookaburra
review.headline: Two Meowfia fell to consensus, then a lone Floofer hugged her way to victory.
review.summary: Round 1 saw Alex's Pigeon bluff die to a simple egg-count check, and the table eggsecuted her. In round 2 Ellis winked Blair and lied about being Hawk, but Kookaburra and Owl reports plus Drew's Turkey denial exposed him. In round 3 Casey the lone Floofer copied a Kookaburra claim, Ellis the real Kookaburra got eggsecuted, and Farm lost. Blair won on a huge round 2 banking of two high cards.

rounds.recap: Alex, a Sphinx, bluffed Pigeon and claimed an egg in Blair's nest, which Blair's dawn report disproved. Everyone threw at Alex and Farm won. Alex threw a Wild at a known Farm player to protect her best card.

Ellis the Mouser claimed Hawk and winked Blair, the real Hawk, mid-day. Casey's Owl report, Alex's Falcon report, Finley's Kookaburra read and Drew's no-visitors Turkey report all pointed at Ellis. Farm won and Blair banked 25 points even though dead.

Casey the Floofer hugged Drew, so Turkey and Falcon did nothing. She claimed Kookaburra, copying the real one, Ellis. Ellis's hug theory was dismissed because Drew's report did not mention a hug, and the table piled on Ellis. Meowfia won with Casey scoring 6.

highlights.text: Alex the Sphinx invented a Pigeon egg that Blair's unchanged nest instantly disproved, and the table locked on her.
Ellis winked Blair mid-day, yet Blair's death only confirmed Blair was dangerous to Meowfia and Farm kept the vote.
Casey copied Ellis's true Kookaburra claim and let the real one be eggsecuted for the same story.
Ellis correctly guessed a Floofer hug explained the zero eggs, but Drew's report showed nothing, so no one believed him.

confusions.what: Claimed Pigeon laid an egg in Blair's nest without a plan for the egg count check, then called the Blair/Drew visit a conflict.
Said nobody visited her based on a +0 egg report, then had to correct that the report only shows eggs.
Doubted Ellis's story by saying Drew had nobody visiting, which is consistent; earlier Casey said Blair's Hawk was contradicted though it was not.
Said her Falcon result contradicted Casey's Owl claim, though both were consistent with Ellis being visited by several players.
Told Drew his Turkey pays the visitor and not him, then treated Drew's claim as suspicious, though Drew had said nothing wrong.
Claimed the dawn report showed no hug, but a hugged player's report says nothing, so the Floofer theory was not refuted.
Argued that two Kookaburra claims were impossible, then called Finley's Hawk consistent with a Tit guess; also treated Ellis's earlier Meowfia role as evidence though roles are re-dealt.
Claimed he gained an egg from visiting Drew the Turkey, but Drew's report showed no visitor, so the Mouser claim was clearly unsupported.

worked: Dawn egg counts versus claims: Alex's fake Pigeon egg in round 1 and Ellis's fake Turkey egg in round 2 were disproved by nest sizes.
The Mouser Wink creating a mid-day death produced a dramatic moment and let dead Blair still bank 25 points.
The Floofer hug in round 3 blanked Turkey and Falcon and made a genuinely hard puzzle for Farm.
Meowfia not knowing each other: Casey and Ellis never competed, and Alex threw at a known Farm player for the consolation card.
problems: Hugged players learn nothing, so the Floofer's effect cannot be proven or disproved; Ellis's correct hug theory was dismissed. Consider a dawn note such as 'something felt off'.
Meowfia lose easily in rounds 1 and 2: bluffs are checked by egg counts and the table converges quickly. Consider a bluff-friendly role or noisier dawn reports.
Throw counts matter little: everyone throws 2 low cards at the consensus target, so there is little risk or decision. Consider rewards for early correct votes.
Scoring snowballs: Blair's 25-point dead throw in round 2 effectively decided the game; the Round 3 outcome was irrelevant to first place. Consider capping a single banked throw or catch-up bonuses.

The Round 3 Kookaburra copy let a lone Meowfia win with one card thrown, because the table preferred a reasoning heuristic over evidence; players also thought re-dealt roles were evidence from earlier rounds.
